title: The future we're building -- and boring
speaker: Elon Musk

sentences.en: Chris Anderson: Elon, hey, welcome back to TED.
sentences.zh: 克里斯·安德森:伊隆,欢迎回到TED。

sentences.en: It's great to have you here. Elon Musk: Thanks for having me.
sentences.zh: 很高兴有你在这里,艾隆・穆斯克:

sentences.en: CA: So, in the next half hour or so, we're going to spend some time exploring your vision for what an exciting future might look like, which I guess makes the first question a little ironic:
sentences.zh: CA: 所以,在接下来的半小时左右, 我们将花一些时间 探究你的愿景 一个令人兴奋的未来可能是什么样子, 我想这使第一个问题 有点讽刺:

sentences.en: Why are you boring? EM: Yeah. I ask myself that frequently.
sentences.zh: 是啊,我经常问自己

sentences.en: We're trying to dig a hole under LA, and this is to create the beginning of what will hopefully be a 3D network of tunnels to alleviate congestion.
sentences.zh: 我们正试图在洛杉矶下面挖一个洞, 这是创造一个开端,希望 将是一个3D隧道网络 来缓解拥挤。

sentences.en: So right now, one of the most soul-destroying things is traffic.
sentences.zh: 所以,现在,最 灵魂毁灭的东西之一是交通。

sentences.en: It affects people in every part of the world.
sentences.zh: 它影响到世界各地人民。

sentences.en: It takes away so much of your life. It's horrible.
sentences.zh: 它夺走了你的很多生命 太可怕了

sentences.en: It's particularly horrible in LA. (Laughter) CA: I think you've brought with you the first visualization that's been shown of this.
sentences.zh: CA:我想你带来了第一个被展示的视觉化。

sentences.en: Can I show this? EM: Yeah, absolutely. So this is the first time -- Just to show what we're talking about.
sentences.zh: 我可以展示这个吗?EM:是的,绝对。所以这是第一次—— 展示我们在谈论的东西。

sentences.en: So a couple of key things that are important in having a 3D tunnel network.
sentences.zh: 因此,一些关键的东西 很重要的3D隧道网络。

sentences.en: First of all, you have to be able to integrate the entrance and exit of the tunnel seamlessly into the fabric of the city.
sentences.zh: 首先,你必须能够把隧道的出入口无缝地融入城市结构。

sentences.en: So by having an elevator, sort of a car skate, that's on an elevator, you can integrate the entrance and exits to the tunnel network
sentences.zh: 有了电梯,车滑板,在电梯上 你可以把隧道网的入口和出口融为一体

sentences.en: just by using two parking spaces. And then the car gets on a skate.
sentences.zh: 只是用两个停车位 然后车就滑了

sentences.en: There's no speed limit here, so we're designing this to be able to operate at 200 kilometers an hour.
sentences.zh: 这里没有限速,所以我们设计这个 能够以每小时200公里的速度运行。

sentences.en: CA: How much? EM: 200 kilometers an hour, or about 130 miles per hour.
sentences.zh: CA:多少钱?EM:每小时200公里,或大约每小时130英里。

sentences.en: So you should be able to get from, say, Westwood to LAX in six minutes -- five, six minutes.
sentences.zh: 所以你应该能在6分钟内 从Westwood到LAX,5,6分钟。

sentences.en: (Applause) CA: So possibly, initially done, it's like on a sort of toll road-type basis.
sentences.zh: (掌声) CA:所以,可能,最初完成, 它就像一种收费 道路类型。

sentences.en: EM: Yeah. CA: Which, I guess, alleviates some traffic from the surface streets as well.
sentences.zh: EM:是的。CA:我想这也缓解了地表街道的交通问题。

sentences.en: EM: So, I don't know if people noticed it in the video, but there's no real limit to how many levels of tunnel you can have.
sentences.zh: EM:所以,我不知道人们是否在视频中注意到它, 但是对于你有多少层的隧道, 并没有真正的限制。

sentences.en: You can go much further deep than you can go up.
sentences.zh: 你可以走得更远 比你可以上去。

sentences.en: The deepest mines are much deeper than the tallest buildings are tall, so you can alleviate any arbitrary level of urban congestion with a 3D tunnel network.
sentences.zh: 最深处的地雷比最高的建筑要深得多, 这样你就可以用3D隧道网络来缓解任何任意的都市拥挤程度。

sentences.en: This is a very important point. So a key rebuttal to the tunnels is that if you add one layer of tunnels, that will simply alleviate congestion, it will get used up, and then you'll be back where you started, back with congestion.
sentences.zh: 这是一个非常重要的点。因此,对隧道的关键反驳是,如果你增加一个隧道层,那只会缓解堵塞,它就会耗尽, 然后你就会回到你开始的地方, 回到堵塞状态。

sentences.en: But you can go to any arbitrary number of tunnels, any number of levels.
sentences.zh: 但是,你可以去任何任意数量的隧道, 任何数量的水平。

sentences.en: CA: But people -- seen traditionally, it's incredibly expensive to dig, and that would block this idea.
sentences.zh: CA:但是人们—— 传统上看,挖掘费用非常昂贵, 这会阻碍这个想法。

sentences.en: EM: Yeah. Well, they're right. To give you an example, the LA subway extension, which is -- I think it's a two-and-a-half mile extension that was just completed for two billion dollars.
sentences.zh: EM:是的。他们说得对。举个例子,洛杉矶地铁的延伸, 就是--我想这是一个2.5英里的延伸, 刚刚完成了20亿美元。

sentences.en: So it's roughly a billion dollars a mile to do the subway extension in LA.
sentences.zh: 因此,它大约10亿美元一英里 做地铁扩展 在洛杉矶。

sentences.en: And this is not the highest utility subway in the world.
sentences.zh: 这不是世界上最高的公用地铁。

sentences.en: So yeah, it's quite difficult to dig tunnels normally.
sentences.zh: 所以,这是相当困难 挖隧道通常。

sentences.en: I think we need to have at least a tenfold improvement in the cost per mile of tunneling.
sentences.zh: 我认为,我们需要至少提高10倍的地道费用。

sentences.en: CA: And how could you achieve that? EM: Actually, if you just do two things, you can get to approximately an order of magnitude improvement, and I think you can go beyond that.
sentences.zh: CA:你怎么能做到这一点呢?EM:实际上,如果你只做两件事, 你可以得到大约一个数量级的改进, 我认为你可以超越这一点。

sentences.en: So the first thing to do is to cut the tunnel diameter by a factor of two or more.
sentences.zh: 所以首先要做的就是把隧道的直径 切成两个或两个以上。

sentences.en: So a single road lane tunnel according to regulations has to be 26 feet, maybe 28 feet in diameter to allow for crashes and emergency vehicles and sufficient ventilation for combustion engine cars.
sentences.zh: 因此,按照规定,一条公路隧道必须达到26英尺,直径可能达到28英尺,以便发生撞车事故和紧急车辆事故,并有足够的通风条件供燃机车使用。

sentences.en: But if you shrink that diameter to what we're attempting, which is 12 feet, which is plenty to get an electric skate through, you drop the diameter by a factor of two and the cross-sectional area by a factor of four,
sentences.zh: 但是如果你将直径缩缩到 我们尝试的12英尺, 足够用电滑板穿透, 你就会把直径降低2倍, 横截面下降4倍,

sentences.en: and the tunneling cost scales with the cross-sectional area.
sentences.zh: 和地道成本表 与横截区。

sentences.en: So that's roughly a half-order of magnitude improvement right there.
sentences.zh: 所以,这是大约半级 规模改善就在那里。

sentences.en: Then tunneling machines currently tunnel for half the time, then they stop, and then the rest of the time is putting in reinforcements for the tunnel wall.
sentences.zh: 然后隧道机器现在有一半的隧道 然后他们停下来 剩下的时间是加固隧道墙

sentences.en: So if you design the machine instead to do continuous tunneling and reinforcing, that will give you a factor of two improvement.
sentences.zh: 所以如果你设计这台机器 来持续地道和加固, 就能改善两个因素。

sentences.en: Combine that and that's a factor of eight.
sentences.zh: 综合起来,这是八个因素。

sentences.en: Also these machines are far from being at their power or thermal limits, so you can jack up the power to the machine substantially.
sentences.zh: 而且这些机器还远未达到它们的电源或热量极限, 所以你可以把电源大量地插到机器上。

sentences.en: I think you can get at least a factor of two, maybe a factor of four or five improvement on top of that.
sentences.zh: 我认为你可以得到至少两个因素, 也许一个因素 四或五个改进。

sentences.en: So I think there's a fairly straightforward series of steps to get somewhere in excess of an order of magnitude improvement in the cost per mile, and our target actually is -- we've got a pet snail called Gary,
sentences.zh: 所以,我认为有一个相当直截了当的系列步骤 到达某个地方 超过一个数量级 改善每英里的成本, 我们实际上的目标是 -- 我们有一个宠物蜗牛 叫做加里,

sentences.en: this is from Gary the snail from "South Park," I mean, sorry, "SpongeBob SquarePants."
sentences.zh: 这是"南方公园"的蜗牛盖瑞的,我是说,对不起,"海绵宝宝广场裤"

sentences.en: (Laughter) So Gary is capable of -- currently he's capable of going 14 times faster than a tunnel-boring machine.
sentences.zh: 所以Gary有能力-- 目前他能跑得比地道机器快14倍。

sentences.en: (Laughter) CA: You want to beat Gary. EM: We want to beat Gary.
sentences.zh: CA:你想打败Gary。EM:我们要打败Gary。

sentences.en: (Laughter) He's not a patient little fellow, and that will be victory.
sentences.zh: (笑) 他不是一个耐心的小家伙, 那将是胜利。

sentences.en: Victory is beating the snail. CA: But a lot of people imagining, dreaming about future cities, they imagine that actually the solution is flying cars, drones, etc.
sentences.zh: 胜利正在战胜蜗牛。CA:但很多人想象, 梦想着未来的城市, 他们想象,实际上解决办法就是 驾驶汽车,无人机,等等。

sentences.en: You go aboveground. Why isn't that a better solution?
sentences.zh: 你到地面上去,为什么不更好呢?

sentences.en: You save all that tunneling cost. EM: Right. I'm in favor of flying things.
sentences.zh: 你节省了所有隧道的费用。EM:对。我赞成飞行的东西。

sentences.en: Obviously, I do rockets, so I like things that fly.
sentences.zh: 显然,我做火箭, 所以我喜欢的东西飞。

sentences.en: This is not some inherent bias against flying things, but there is a challenge with flying cars in that they'll be quite noisy, the wind force generated will be very high.
sentences.zh: 这并不是对飞行物体的固有偏见，而是飞行汽车面临的挑战，因为它们会非常吵闹，产生的风力会非常大。

sentences.en: Let's just say that if something's flying over your head, a whole bunch of flying cars going all over the place, that is not an anxiety-reducing situation.
sentences.zh: 这么说吧，如果有什么东西从你头顶飞过，一大堆飞行汽车到处乱跑，这并不是一种可以减轻焦虑的情况。

sentences.en: (Laughter) You don't think to yourself, "Well, I feel better about today."
sentences.zh: （笑声）你不会对自己说：“嗯，我今天感觉好多了。”

sentences.en: You're thinking, "Did they service their hubcap, or is it going to come off and guillotine me?"
sentences.zh: 你会想，“他们的轮毂盖保养了吗？还是轮毂盖会脱落，把我送上断头台？”

sentences.en: Things like that. CA: So you've got this vision of future cities with these rich, 3D networks of tunnels underneath.
sentences.zh: 诸如此类的事情。 CA：所以你已经看到了未来城市的愿景，其地下有丰富的 3D 隧道网络。

sentences.en: Is there a tie-in here with Hyperloop? Could you apply these tunnels to use for this Hyperloop idea you released a few years ago.
sentences.zh: 这与超级高铁有关联吗？您能否将这些隧道应用于您几年前发布的超级高铁想法？

sentences.en: EM: Yeah, so we've been sort of puttering around with the Hyperloop stuff for a while.
sentences.zh: EM：是的，所以我们已经在超级高铁方面闲逛了一段时间了。

sentences.en: We built a Hyperloop test track adjacent to SpaceX, just for a student competition, to encourage innovative ideas in transport.
sentences.zh: 我们在 SpaceX 附近建造了一条超级高铁测试轨道，专门用于学生竞赛，以鼓励运输方面的创新想法。

sentences.en: And it actually ends up being the biggest vacuum chamber in the world after the Large Hadron Collider, by volume.
sentences.zh: 事实上，按体积计算，它最终成为继大型强子对撞机之后世界上最大的真空室。

sentences.en: So it was quite fun to do that, but it was kind of a hobby thing, and then we think we might -- so we've built a little pusher car to push the student pods,
sentences.zh: 所以这样做很有趣，但这是一种爱好，然后我们认为我们可以 - 所以我们建造了一辆小推车来推动学生舱，

sentences.en: but we're going to try seeing how fast we can make the pusher go if it's not pushing something.
sentences.zh: 但我们将尝试看看如果推动器不推动某物，我们可以让推动器移动多快。

sentences.en: So we're cautiously optimistic we'll be able to be faster than the world's fastest bullet train even in a .8-mile stretch.
sentences.zh: 因此，我们谨慎乐观地认为，即使在 0.8 英里的路程中，我们也能比世界上最快的子弹头列车更快。

sentences.en: CA: Whoa. Good brakes. EM: Yeah, I mean, it's -- yeah.
sentences.zh: CA：哇哦。刹车好。 EM：是的，我的意思是，是的。

sentences.en: It's either going to smash into tiny pieces or go quite fast.
sentences.zh: 它要么会碎成小碎片，要么飞得很快。

sentences.en: CA: But you can picture, then, a Hyperloop in a tunnel running quite long distances.
sentences.zh: CA：但是你可以想象，超级高铁在隧道中运行相当长的距离。

sentences.en: EM: Exactly. And looking at tunneling technology, it turns out that in order to make a tunnel, you have to -- In order to seal against the water table, you've got to typically design a tunnel wall to be good
sentences.zh: 埃姆：没错。看看隧道技术，事实证明，为了建造隧道，你必须——为了密封地下水位，你通常必须设计一个良好的隧道墙

sentences.en: to about five or six atmospheres. So to go to vacuum is only one atmosphere, or near-vacuum.
sentences.zh: 大约五到六个大气压。所以真空只是一个大气压，或者接近真空。

sentences.en: So actually, it sort of turns out that automatically, if you build a tunnel that is good enough to resist the water table, it is automatically capable of holding vacuum.
sentences.zh: 所以实际上，事实证明，如果你建造了一条足以抵抗地下水位的隧道，它就自动能够保持真空。

sentences.en: CA: Huh. EM: So, yeah. CA: And so you could actually picture, what kind of length tunnel is in Elon's future to running Hyperloop?
sentences.zh: 加州：嗯。 EM：所以，是的。 CA：所以你实际上可以想象，埃隆未来运行超级高铁的隧道长度是多少？

sentences.en: EM: I think there's no real length limit.
sentences.zh: EM：我认为没有实际长度限制。

sentences.en: You could dig as much as you want. I think if you were to do something like a DC-to-New York Hyperloop, I think you'd probably want to go underground the entire way
sentences.zh: 你想挖多少就挖多少。我想如果你要做像华盛顿到纽约的超级高铁这样的事情，我想你可能会想全程进入地下

sentences.en: because it's a high-density area. You're going under a lot of buildings and houses, and if you go deep enough, you cannot detect the tunnel.
sentences.zh: 因为这是一个高密度区域。你要进入很多建筑物和房屋的下面，如果你走得足够深，你就无法探测到隧道。

sentences.en: Sometimes people think, well, it's going to be pretty annoying to have a tunnel dug under my house.
sentences.zh: 有时人们会想，好吧，在我的房子下面挖一条隧道会很烦人。

sentences.en: Like, if that tunnel is dug more than about three or four tunnel diameters beneath your house, you will not be able to detect it being dug at all.
sentences.zh: 例如，如果该隧道在您房屋下方挖掘的直径超过三到四个隧道直径，您将根本无法检测到它正在挖掘。

sentences.en: In fact, if you're able to detect the tunnel being dug, whatever device you are using, you can get a lot of money for that device from the Israeli military, who is trying to detect tunnels from Hamas,
sentences.zh: 事实上，如果你能够检测到正在挖掘的隧道，无论你使用什么设备，你都可以从以色列军方那里获得很多钱来购买该设备，以色列军方正试图检测来自哈马斯的隧道，

sentences.en: and from the US Customs and Border patrol that try and detect drug tunnels.
sentences.zh: 以及来自美国海关和边境巡逻 试图检测毒品隧道。

sentences.en: So the reality is that earth is incredibly good at absorbing vibrations, and once the tunnel depth is below a certain level, it is undetectable.
sentences.zh: 现实是,地球非常擅长吸收振动, 一旦隧道深度低于一定水平, 就无法探测到。

sentences.en: Maybe if you have a very sensitive seismic instrument, you might be able to detect it.
sentences.zh: 也许如果你有一个非常敏感的地震仪器, 你也许能够检测到它。

sentences.en: CA: So you've started a new company to do this called The Boring Company.
sentences.zh: CA:所以你成立了一家新的公司 来做这个叫做波音公司。

sentences.en: Very nice. Very funny. (Laughter) EM: What's funny about that?
sentences.zh: 很好,很好笑,有什么好笑的吗?

sentences.en: (Laughter) CA: How much of your time is this?
sentences.zh: CA:你有多少时间了?

sentences.en: EM: It's maybe ... two or three percent.
sentences.zh: EM:也许... 百分之二或百分之三。

sentences.en: CA: You've called it a hobby. This is what an Elon Musk hobby looks like.
sentences.zh: CA:你把它称为爱好。这就是Elon Musk的爱好。

sentences.en: (Laughter) EM: I mean, it really is, like -- This is basically interns and people doing it part time.
sentences.zh: (笑声) EM:我的意思是,这真的是,就像——这基本上是实习生和做兼职的人。

sentences.en: We bought some second-hand machinery. It's kind of puttering along, but it's making good progress, so -- CA: So an even bigger part of your time is being spent on electrifying cars and transport through Tesla.
sentences.zh: 我们买了一些二手机器。这有点复杂, 但它正在取得良好的进展, 所以,CA:所以你的更多时间 花在了电动汽车上 和通过特斯拉的交通上。

sentences.en: Is one of the motivations for the tunneling project the realization that actually, in a world where cars are electric and where they're self-driving, there may end up being more cars on the roads
sentences.zh: 是隧道工程的动机之一 即意识到,实际上, 在世界上,汽车是电动的 和他们自己驾驶, 最终可能会有更多的汽车在路上

sentences.en: on any given hour than there are now? EM: Yeah, exactly.
sentences.zh: 时间比现在还长吗?

sentences.en: A lot of people think that when you make cars autonomous, they'll be able to go faster and that will alleviate congestion.
sentences.zh: 很多人认为,当你使汽车自治, 他们能够走得更快,这将缓解拥堵。

sentences.en: And to some degree that will be true, but once you have shared autonomy where it's much cheaper to go by car and you can go point to point, the affordability of going in a car will be better than that of a bus.
sentences.zh: 在某种程度上,这是真的, 但一旦你拥有了共享的自主权 在那里,它的成本要低得多, 你可以指出这一点, 乘坐汽车的可负担性 比公共汽车的好。

sentences.en: Like, it will cost less than a bus ticket.
sentences.zh: 喜欢,它的成本将低于公共汽车票。

sentences.en: So the amount of driving that will occur will be much greater with shared autonomy, and actually traffic will get far worse.
sentences.zh: 因此,随着共同自主性的发展,驾驶量将会大得多,实际上交通量会大得多。

sentences.en: CA: You started Tesla with the goal of persuading the world that electrification was the future of cars, and a few years ago, people were laughing at you.
sentences.zh: CA:你启动Tesla的目的是说服世界 电气化是汽车的未来, 几年前,人们嘲笑你。

sentences.en: Now, not so much. EM: OK. (Laughter) I don't know. I don't know.
sentences.zh: 现在,不要太多。 EM:好吧。我不知道。我不知道。

sentences.en: CA: But isn't it true that pretty much every auto manufacturer has announced serious electrification plans for the short- to medium-term future?
sentences.zh: CA:但难道不是每个汽车制造商都宣布了 短期到中期的电气化计划吗?

sentences.en: EM: Yeah. I think almost every automaker has some electric vehicle program.
sentences.zh: EM:是的,我想几乎每个汽车制造商都有电动汽车程序。

sentences.en: They vary in seriousness. Some are very serious about transitioning entirely to electric, and some are just dabbling in it.
sentences.zh: 他们的严肃性各不相同。有些人对完全转向电机非常认真,有些人只是纠缠在电机上。

sentences.en: And some, amazingly, are still pursuing fuel cells, but I think that won't last much longer.
sentences.zh: 有些人,令人惊讶的是, 还在追求燃料电池, 但我认为这不会持续太久。

sentences.en: CA: But isn't there a sense, though, Elon, where you can now just declare victory and say, you know, "We did it."
sentences.zh: CA:不过,Elon,你难道没有感觉吗? 你可以在这里宣布胜利,然后说,“我们做到了。”

sentences.en: Let the world electrify, and you go on and focus on other stuff?
sentences.zh: 让世界通电,然后你继续关注其他事情?

sentences.en: EM: Yeah. I intend to stay with Tesla as far into the future as I can imagine, and there are a lot of exciting things that we have coming.
sentences.zh: EM:是的。我打算和Tesla呆在一起, 直至未来,我可以想象, 有很多令人兴奋的事情, 我们来了。

sentences.en: Obviously the Model 3 is coming soon. We'll be unveiling the Tesla Semi truck.
sentences.zh: 明显3号机马上就要到了 我们要揭开Tesla Semi卡车

sentences.en: CA: OK, we're going to come to this. So Model 3, it's supposed to be coming in July-ish.
sentences.zh: CA:好的,我们来谈这个。3号模型应该是7月到的。

sentences.en: EM: Yeah, it's looking quite good for starting production in July.
sentences.zh: EM:7月份开始生产看起来不错。

sentences.en: CA: Wow. One of the things that people are so excited about is the fact that it's got autopilot.
sentences.zh: CA:哇。人们如此兴奋的一件事是 它有自动驾驶。

sentences.en: And you put out this video a while back showing what that technology would look like.
sentences.zh: 你放出这段视频 展示出这个技术会是什么样子

sentences.en: EM: Yeah. CA: There's obviously autopilot in Model S right now.
sentences.zh: EM:是的。CA:现在显然有S型自动驾驶。

sentences.en: What are we seeing here? EM: Yeah, so this is using only cameras and GPS.
sentences.zh: 我们在这里看到了什么?EM:是的,所以这只使用相机和GPS。

sentences.en: So there's no LIDAR or radar being used here.
sentences.zh: 所以这里没有使用LIDAR或雷达

sentences.en: This is just using passive optical, which is essentially what a person uses.
sentences.zh: 这只是使用被动光学, 这基本上是一个人使用的。

sentences.en: The whole road system is meant to be navigated with passive optical, or cameras, and so once you solve cameras or vision, then autonomy is solved.
sentences.zh: 整个道路系统都是用被动的光学或摄像头导航的, 所以一旦你破解了摄像头或视觉, 自治就解决了。

sentences.en: If you don't solve vision, it's not solved.
sentences.zh: 如果你不解决幻觉, 它不是解决。

sentences.en: So that's why our focus is so heavily on having a vision neural net that's very effective for road conditions.
sentences.zh: 所以,这就是为什么我们如此关注 拥有一个视觉神经网 对道路状况非常有效。

sentences.en: CA: Right. Many other people are going the LIDAR route.
sentences.zh: CA:没错,还有很多人走LIDAR路线。

sentences.en: You want cameras plus radar is most of it.
sentences.zh: 你想要摄像头加上雷达是大部分

sentences.en: EM: You can absolutely be superhuman with just cameras.
sentences.zh: EM:只要有摄像头,你绝对可以成为超人。

sentences.en: Like, you can probably do it ten times better than humans would, just cameras.
sentences.zh: 比如,你可能比人类做的好十倍,只是摄像头

sentences.en: CA: So the new cars being sold right now have eight cameras in them.
sentences.zh: CA:所以现在出售的新车里面有八台摄像机。

sentences.en: They can't yet do what that showed. When will they be able to?
sentences.zh: 他们现在还不能做所显示的 他们什么时候才能做?

sentences.en: EM: I think we're still on track for being able to go cross-country from LA to New York by the end of the year, fully autonomous.
sentences.zh: EM:我想我们还是可以 在今年年底从洛杉矶到纽约的, 完全自治的。

sentences.en: CA: OK, so by the end of the year, you're saying, someone's going to sit in a Tesla without touching the steering wheel, tap in "New York," off it goes.
sentences.zh: CA:好吧,所以到年底, 你说,有人会坐在特斯拉 不触动方向盘, 敲在“纽约”,它去。

sentences.en: EM: Yeah. CA: Won't ever have to touch the wheel -- by the end of 2017.
sentences.zh: EM:是的。CA:到2017年底, 永远不用碰方向盘。

sentences.en: EM: Yeah. Essentially, November or December of this year, we should be able to go all the way from a parking lot in California to a parking lot in New York, no controls touched at any point during the entire journey.
sentences.zh: EM:是的。基本上,今年11月或12月, 我们应该能够一路 从加利福尼亚州的一个停车场到纽约的一个停车场, 在整个旅程中, 没有任何控制点被触动。

sentences.en: (Applause) CA: Amazing. But part of that is possible because you've already got a fleet of Teslas driving all these roads.
sentences.zh: (掌声) CA:太神奇了。但其中的一部分是可能的, 因为你已经得到了一个车队 特斯拉斯驾驶所有这些道路。

sentences.en: You're accumulating a huge amount of data of that national road system.
sentences.zh: 你积累了大量关于国家道路系统的数据

sentences.en: EM: Yes, but the thing that will be interesting is that I'm actually fairly confident it will be able to do that route even if you change the route dynamically.
sentences.zh: EM:是的,但有趣的是, 我确实相当有信心 它能够做这条路线 即使你动态地改变路线。

sentences.en: So, it's fairly easy -- If you say I'm going to be really good at one specific route, that's one thing, but it should be able to go, really be very good,
sentences.zh: 所以,这是相当容易的——如果你说我会在一条特定的路线上 做得很好,那是一回事, 但是它应该可以去, 真的非常好,

sentences.en: certainly once you enter a highway, to go anywhere on the highway system in a given country.
sentences.zh: 当然,一旦你进入高速公路, 去任何地方的高速公路系统 在特定的国家。

sentences.en: So it's not sort of limited to LA to New York.
sentences.zh: 所以它并不局限于洛杉矶到纽约

sentences.en: We could change it and make it Seattle-Florida, that day, in real time.
sentences.zh: 我们可以改变它 并使它西雅图 -弗洛里达, 那一天,实时。

sentences.en: So you were going from LA to New York. Now go from LA to Toronto.
sentences.zh: 所以你从洛杉矶到纽约 现在从洛杉矶到多伦多

sentences.en: CA: So leaving aside regulation for a second, in terms of the technology alone, the time when someone will be able to buy one of your cars and literally just take the hands off the wheel and go to sleep
sentences.zh: CA:所以把监管权放在一边, 就技术而言, 当有人能够买你的一辆车的时候, 并且干脆把手从轮子上拿开,然后睡觉

sentences.en: and wake up and find that they've arrived, how far away is that, to do that safely?
sentences.zh: 醒来发现他们已经到达了, 离这有多远, 安全地做到这一点?

sentences.en: EM: I think that's about two years. So the real trick of it is not how do you make it work say 99.9 percent of the time, because, like, if a car crashes one in a thousand times,
sentences.zh: EM:我想这大概是两年了。所以真正的技巧不是 如何让它工作 说99.9%的时间, 因为,像,如果汽车撞车 一千次,

sentences.en: then you're probably still not going to be comfortable falling asleep.
sentences.zh: 那你可能还是睡不着觉

sentences.en: You shouldn't be, certainly. (Laughter) It's never going to be perfect.
sentences.zh: 你不应该是,当然。 它永远不会是完美的。

sentences.en: No system is going to be perfect, but if you say it's perhaps -- the car is unlikely to crash in a hundred lifetimes, or a thousand lifetimes, then people are like, OK, wow, if I were to live a thousand lives,
sentences.zh: 没有一个系统会是完美的, 但是如果你说它可能是—— 汽车不可能在100个生命中坠毁, 或者千个生命中坠毁, 那么人们就像,好吧,哇,如果我能活上一千个生命,

sentences.en: I would still most likely never experience a crash, then that's probably OK.
sentences.zh: 我可能永远也不会遇到撞车,那也没关系。

sentences.en: CA: To sleep. I guess the big concern of yours is that people may actually get seduced too early to think that this is safe, and that you'll have some horrible incident happen that puts things back.
sentences.zh: CA:睡觉。我想你最关心的是 人们可能真的被引诱得太早 以为这是安全的, 而且你会发生一些可怕的事件 使事情倒退。

sentences.en: EM: Well, I think that the autonomy system is likely to at least mitigate the crash, except in rare circumstances.
sentences.zh: EM:我认为自治制度至少可以缓解崩溃,除非在罕见的情况下。

sentences.en: The thing to appreciate about vehicle safety is this is probabilistic.
sentences.zh: 欣赏车辆安全性的原因是,这是概率。

sentences.en: I mean, there's some chance that any time a human driver gets in a car, that they will have an accident that is their fault.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是,有某种可能性, 任何时候,一个人驾驶员 上车, 他们将有一个事故,这是他们的错。

sentences.en: It's never zero. So really the key threshold for autonomy is how much better does autonomy need to be than a person before you can rely on it?
sentences.zh: 它从不为零。因此,自治的关键门槛是,在你能够依赖它之前,自治需要比一个人更好吗?

sentences.en: CA: But once you get literally safe hands-off driving, the power to disrupt the whole industry seems massive, because at that point you've spoken of people being able to buy a car, drops you off at work, and then you let it go
sentences.zh: CA:但一旦你得到 真正安全的手动驾驶, 破坏整个行业的力量 似乎巨大的, 因为当时你说过 人们可以买车,

sentences.en: and provide a sort of Uber-like service to other people, earn you money, maybe even cover the cost of your lease of that car, so you can kind of get a car for free.
sentences.zh: 并且为其他人提供类似Uber的服务, 赚你的钱, 甚至可能支付你租车的费用, 这样你就可以免费得到一辆车。

sentences.en: Is that really likely? EM: Yeah. Absolutely this is what will happen.
sentences.zh: 是的 绝对是这样的

sentences.en: So there will be a shared autonomy fleet where you buy your car and you can choose to use that car exclusively, you could choose to have it be used only by friends and family, only by other drivers who are rated five star,
sentences.zh: 因此,将有一个共享的自治车队 在那里,你买你的车 你可以选择使用这辆车 完全,你可以选择有 它只有朋友和家人, 只有其他司机 谁被评为五星级,

sentences.en: you can choose to share it sometimes but not other times.
sentences.zh: 你可以选择分享它 有时,但不要其他时间。

sentences.en: That's 100 percent what will occur. It's just a question of when.
sentences.zh: 百分百会发生,只是时间问题

sentences.en: CA: Wow. So you mentioned the Semi and I think you're planning to announce this in September, but I'm curious whether there's anything you could show us today?
sentences.zh: CA:哇。你提到"半"了,我想你打算9月宣布这个, 但我想知道你今天能不能给我们看点什么?

sentences.en: EM: I will show you a teaser shot of the truck.
sentences.zh: EM:我会给你看卡车的滑稽镜头。

sentences.en: (Laughter) It's alive. CA: OK. EM: That's definitely a case where we want to be cautious about the autonomy features.
sentences.zh: （笑声）它还活着。加州：好的。 EM：这绝对是我们要对自主功能保持谨慎的情况。

sentences.en: Yeah. (Laughter) CA: We can't see that much of it, but it doesn't look like just a little friendly neighborhood truck.
sentences.zh: 是的。 （笑声） CA：我们看不到那么多，但它看起来并不只是一辆友好的邻家小卡车。

sentences.en: It looks kind of badass. What sort of semi is this?
sentences.zh: 看起来有点坏蛋。这是什么类型的半？

sentences.en: EM: So this is a heavy duty, long-range semitruck.
sentences.zh: EM：这是一辆重型远程半挂卡车。

sentences.en: So it's the highest weight capability and with long range.
sentences.zh: 因此它具有最高的重量能力和较远的射程。

sentences.en: So essentially it's meant to alleviate the heavy-duty trucking loads.
sentences.zh: 所以本质上它是为了减轻重型卡车运输的负载。

sentences.en: And this is something which people do not today think is possible.
sentences.zh: 今天人们认为这是不可能的。

sentences.en: They think the truck doesn't have enough power or it doesn't have enough range, and then with the Tesla Semi we want to show that no, an electric truck actually can out-torque any diesel semi.
sentences.zh: 他们认为卡车没有足够的动力或者没有足够的行驶里程，然后通过特斯拉半挂车，我们想证明，不，电动卡车实际上可以超过任何柴油半挂车的扭矩。

sentences.en: And if you had a tug-of-war competition, the Tesla Semi will tug the diesel semi uphill.
sentences.zh: 如果您进行拔河比赛，特斯拉半挂车将拖着柴油半挂车上坡。

sentences.en: (Laughter) (Applause) CA: That's pretty cool. And short term, these aren't driverless.
sentences.zh: （笑声）（掌声） CA：那太酷了。从短期来看，这些都不是无人驾驶的。

sentences.en: These are going to be trucks that truck drivers want to drive.
sentences.zh: 这些将是卡车司机想要驾驶的卡车。

sentences.en: EM: Yes. So what will be really fun about this is you have a flat torque RPM curve with an electric motor, whereas with a diesel motor or any kind of internal combustion engine car, you've got a torque RPM curve that looks like a hill.
sentences.zh: 埃姆：是的。因此，真正有趣的是，使用电动机时，您会得到平坦的扭矩 RPM 曲线，而使用柴油发动机或任何类型的内燃机汽车时，您会得到看起来像小山的扭矩 RPM 曲线。

sentences.en: So this will be a very spry truck. You can drive this around like a sports car.
sentences.zh: 所以这将是一辆非常灵活的卡车。您可以像跑车一样驾驶它。

sentences.en: There's no gears. It's, like, single speed.
sentences.zh: 没有齿轮。就像单速一样。

sentences.en: CA: There's a great movie to be made here somewhere.
sentences.zh: CA：这里有一部很棒的电影要拍。

sentences.en: I don't know what it is and I don't know that it ends well, but it's a great movie.
sentences.zh: 我不知道它是什么，也不知道它的结局是否好，但这是一部很棒的电影。

sentences.en: (Laughter) EM: It's quite bizarre test-driving.
sentences.zh: （笑声） EM：这是一次相当奇怪的试驾。

sentences.en: When I was driving the test prototype for the first truck.
sentences.zh: 当我驾驶第一辆卡车的测试原型时。

sentences.en: It's really weird, because you're driving around and you're just so nimble, and you're in this giant truck.
sentences.zh: 这真的很奇怪，因为你开车到处走，而且你非常灵活，而且你在这辆巨大的卡车里。

sentences.en: CA: Wait, you've already driven a prototype?
sentences.zh: CA：等等，你已经驾驶过原型车了吗？

sentences.en: EM: Yeah, I drove it around the parking lot, and I was like, this is crazy.
sentences.zh: EM：是的，我开着它在停车场转了一圈，我想，这太疯狂了。

sentences.en: CA: Wow. This is no vaporware. EM: It's just like, driving this giant truck and making these mad maneuvers.
sentences.zh: 加州：哇。这不是汽件。 EM：就像驾驶这辆巨型卡车并进行这些疯狂的操作一样。

sentences.en: CA: This is cool. OK, from a really badass picture to a kind of less badass picture.
sentences.zh: CA：这很酷。好吧，从一张非常糟糕的照片到一张不那么糟糕的照片。

sentences.en: This is just a cute house from "Desperate Housewives" or something.
sentences.zh: 这只是《绝望的主妇》之类的可爱的房子。

sentences.en: What on earth is going on here? EM: Well, this illustrates the picture of the future that I think is how things will evolve.
sentences.zh: 这里到底发生了什么？ EM：嗯，这描绘了我认为事物将如何演变的未来图景。

sentences.en: You've got an electric car in the driveway.
sentences.zh: 车道上有电动车

sentences.en: If you look in between the electric car and the house, there are actually three Powerwalls stacked up against the side of the house, and then that house roof is a solar roof.
sentences.zh: 如果你看看电动车和房子之间, 实际上有三个电动墙堆在房子的一侧, 然后房子的屋顶是太阳能屋顶。

sentences.en: So that's an actual solar glass roof. CA: OK.
sentences.zh: 这就是真正的太阳玻璃屋顶。CA:好吧。

sentences.en: EM: That's a picture of a real -- well, admittedly, it's a real fake house.
sentences.zh: EM:这是一张真实的照片-- 嗯,承认,这是一个真正的假房子。

sentences.en: That's a real fake house. (Laughter) CA: So these roof tiles, some of them have in them basically solar power, the ability to --
sentences.zh: 所以这些屋顶的瓷砖, 其中一些基本上有太阳能, 有能力...

sentences.en: EM: Yeah. Solar glass tiles where you can adjust the texture and the color to a very fine-grained level, and then there's sort of microlouvers in the glass,
sentences.zh: EM:是的。太阳玻璃瓷砖, 你可以把质地和颜色调整到一个非常细微的水平, 然后在玻璃里有某种微粒,

sentences.en: such that when you're looking at the roof from street level or close to street level, all the tiles look the same whether there is a solar cell behind it or not.
sentences.zh: 当你从街上或接近街上看屋顶时, 所有的瓷砖看起来都是一样的, 不论后面是否有太阳能电池。

sentences.en: So you have an even color from the ground level.
sentences.zh: 所以,你有一个均衡的颜色 从地面一级。

sentences.en: If you were to look at it from a helicopter, you would be actually able to look through and see that some of the glass tiles have a solar cell behind them and some do not.
sentences.zh: 如果你从直升机上看到它, 你会看到一些玻璃砖后面有一个太阳能电池, 有些没有。

sentences.en: You can't tell from street level. CA: You put them in the ones that are likely to see a lot of sun, and that makes these roofs super affordable, right?
sentences.zh: CA:你把它们放在那些 可能看到太阳的地方, 使这些屋顶变得非常便宜,对吗?

sentences.en: They're not that much more expensive than just tiling the roof.
sentences.zh: 他们没那么贵 比只是铺屋顶。

sentences.en: EM: Yeah. We're very confident that the cost of the roof plus the cost of electricity -- A solar glass roof will be less than the cost of a normal roof
sentences.zh: EM:是的。我们非常相信 屋顶的费用加上电费—— 太阳能玻璃屋顶的费用 将低于普通屋顶的费用。

sentences.en: plus the cost of electricity. So in other words, this will be economically a no-brainer, we think it will look great, and it will last -- We thought about having the warranty be infinity,
sentences.zh: 加上电费。换句话说,这在经济上是无脑的, 我们认为它看起来很棒, 并且会持续—— 我们考虑保证是无限的。

sentences.en: but then people thought, well, that might sound like were just talking rubbish, but actually this is toughened glass.
sentences.zh: 但后来人们想,嗯,这听起来像是在胡说八道, 但实际上这是坚固的玻璃。

sentences.en: Well after the house has collapsed and there's nothing there, the glass tiles will still be there.
sentences.zh: 房子倒塌后,那里什么都没有 玻璃瓷砖还在那里

sentences.en: (Applause) CA: I mean, this is cool. So you're rolling this out in a couple week's time, I think, with four different roofing types.
sentences.zh: (掌声) CA:我的意思是,这是很酷的。所以你在几个星期后,我想, 四个不同的屋顶类型。

sentences.en: EM: Yeah, we're starting off with two, two initially, and the second two will be introduced early next year.
sentences.zh: EM:是的,我们开始 以二,二,第二 将在明年初推出。

sentences.en: CA: And what's the scale of ambition here?
sentences.zh: CA: 抱负的规模是什么?

sentences.en: How many houses do you believe could end up having this type of roofing?
sentences.zh: 你相信有多少房子 最终会有这种屋顶?

sentences.en: EM: I think eventually almost all houses will have a solar roof.
sentences.zh: EM:我想几乎所有的房子最终都会有一个太阳能屋顶。

sentences.en: The thing is to consider the time scale here to be probably on the order of 40 or 50 years.
sentences.zh: 关键是考虑一下这里的时间范围 大约是40到50年

sentences.en: So on average, a roof is replaced every 20 to 25 years.
sentences.zh: 平均而言,屋顶每20到25年更换一次。

sentences.en: But you don't start replacing all roofs immediately.
sentences.zh: 但你不能马上换掉所有屋顶

sentences.en: But eventually, if you say were to fast-forward to say 15 years from now, it will be unusual to have a roof that does not have solar.
sentences.zh: 但最终,如果你说15年后要快速前进, 拥有一个没有太阳能的屋顶是不寻常的。

sentences.en: CA: Is there a mental model thing that people don't get here that because of the shift in the cost, the economics of solar power, most houses actually have enough sunlight on their roof pretty much to power all of their needs.
sentences.zh: CA: 是否有一种心理模型,人们不在这里 因为成本的变化, 太阳能的经济, 大部分房屋实际上有足够的阳光 在他们的屋顶上 几乎可以满足他们的需要。

sentences.en: If you could capture the power, it could pretty much power all their needs.
sentences.zh: 如果你能捕捉到能量, 它几乎可以 动力所有他们的需求。

sentences.en: You could go off-grid, kind of. EM: It depends on where you are and what the house size is relative to the roof area, but it's a fair statement to say that most houses in the US have enough roof area
sentences.zh: 你可以离开电网,比如说。EM:这取决于你在哪里,房子大小与屋顶面积的相对关系,但说美国大多数房屋有足够的屋顶面积是公平的。

sentences.en: to power all the needs of the house. CA: So the key to the economics of the cars, the Semi, of these houses is the falling price of lithium-ion batteries,
sentences.zh: CA: 汽车经济学的关键是 锂离子电池价格的下跌

sentences.en: which you've made a huge bet on as Tesla.
sentences.zh: 你以特斯拉的名号下赌注

sentences.en: In many ways, that's almost the core competency.
sentences.zh: 在许多方面,这几乎是核心能力。

sentences.en: And you've decided that to really, like, own that competency, you just have to build the world's largest manufacturing plant to double the world's supply of lithium-ion batteries,
sentences.zh: 你决定 要真正拥有这种能力 你只需要建造世界上最大的制造厂 将全世界的锂离子电池供应量翻一番

sentences.en: with this guy. What is this? EM: Yeah, so that's the Gigafactory, progress so far on the Gigafactory.
sentences.zh: 这是Gigafactory,到目前为止的进展。

sentences.en: Eventually, you can sort of roughly see that there's sort of a diamond shape overall, and when it's fully done, it'll look like a giant diamond, or that's the idea behind it, and it's aligned on true north.
sentences.zh: 最终,你可以大致地看到 某种钻石形状的整体, 当它完全完成, 它会看起来像一个巨型钻石, 或者这就是它背后的想法, 并且它与真实的北方接轨。

sentences.en: It's a small detail. CA: And capable of producing, eventually, like a hundred gigawatt hours of batteries a year.
sentences.zh: 这个小细节。CA:最终, 能够生产100千兆瓦的电池。

sentences.en: EM: A hundred gigawatt hours. We think probably more, but yeah.
sentences.zh: EM: 100千兆瓦小时。我们可能考虑更多,但是是的。

sentences.en: CA: And they're actually being produced right now.
sentences.zh: CA:现在它们正在生产。

sentences.en: EM: They're in production already. CA: You guys put out this video.
sentences.zh: EM:他们已经在制作了。CA:你们把视频放出来了。

sentences.en: I mean, is that speeded up? EM: That's the slowed down version.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是,这是加速的吗?

sentences.en: (Laughter) CA: How fast does it actually go?
sentences.zh: (笑声) CA:它到底跑多快?

sentences.en: EM: Well, when it's running at full speed, you can't actually see the cells without a strobe light.
sentences.zh: EM: 嗯,当它以全速运行时, 你无法真正看到没有光线的细胞。

sentences.en: It's just blur. (Laughter) CA: One of your core ideas, Elon, about what makes an exciting future is a future where we no longer feel guilty about energy.
sentences.zh: (笑声) CA:你的核心想法之一,伊隆, 是什么使一个令人振奋的未来 是一个我们不再对能源感到内疚的未来。

sentences.en: Help us picture this. How many Gigafactories, if you like, does it take to get us there?
sentences.zh: 帮我们想象一下 如果你愿意的话 有多少个Gigafactories 能让我们到那里去吗?

sentences.en: EM: It's about a hundred, roughly. It's not 10, it's not a thousand.
sentences.zh: EM:大约是100个,不是10个,不是1000个。

sentences.en: Most likely a hundred. CA: See, I find this amazing.
sentences.zh: 很可能是一百个。你看,我觉得这很棒。

sentences.en: You can picture what it would take to move the world off this vast fossil fuel thing.
sentences.zh: 你可以想象让世界摆脱这种巨大的化石燃料需要什么。

sentences.en: It's like you're building one, it costs five billion dollars, or whatever, five to 10 billion dollars.
sentences.zh: 就像你在建一个, 它花费了50亿美元, 或什么的, 5到100亿美元。

sentences.en: Like, it's kind of cool that you can picture that project.
sentences.zh: 喜欢,它是一种很酷的 你可以想象那个项目。

sentences.en: And you're planning to do, at Tesla -- announce another two this year.
sentences.zh: 你计划今年在特斯拉再宣布两次

sentences.en: EM: I think we'll announce locations for somewhere between two and four Gigafactories later this year.
sentences.zh: EM:今年晚些时候,我们将宣布 介于2到4个Gigafactories之间的地点。

sentences.en: Yeah, probably four. CA: Whoa. (Applause) No more teasing from you for here?
sentences.zh: 是啊,大概4个。 CA: 哇。

sentences.en: Like -- where, continent? You can say no.
sentences.zh: 比如说,哪里,大陆?

sentences.en: EM: We need to address a global market. CA: OK.
sentences.zh: EM:我们需要处理一个全球市场。CA:好的。

sentences.en: (Laughter) This is cool. I think we should talk for -- Actually, global market.
sentences.zh: (笑声)这很酷。我想我们应该谈谈,实际上,全球市场。

sentences.en: I'm going to ask you one question about politics, only one.
sentences.zh: 我问你一个政治问题 只有一个问题

sentences.en: I'm kind of sick of politics, but I do want to ask you this.
sentences.zh: 我有点厌烦政治 但我想问你这个

sentences.en: You're on a body now giving advice to a guy -- EM: Who?
sentences.zh: 你在身体上 给一个人提供建议 - EM:谁?

sentences.en: CA: Who has said he doesn't really believe in climate change, and there's a lot of people out there who think you shouldn't be doing that.
sentences.zh: CA:谁说过他不相信气候变化, 外面有很多人认为你不应该这样做。

sentences.en: They'd like you to walk away from that. What would you say to them?
sentences.zh: 他们希望你离开,你会跟他们说什么?

sentences.en: EM: Well, I think that first of all, I'm just on two advisory councils where the format consists of going around the room and asking people's opinion on things, and so there's like a meeting every month or two.
sentences.zh: EM:嗯,我想首先,我只是在两个咨询理事会, 其形式是 环绕房间 并询问人们对事情的意见, 所以有像一个会议 每个月或两个月。

sentences.en: That's the sum total of my contribution.
sentences.zh: 这是我贡献的总和

sentences.en: But I think to the degree that there are people in the room who are arguing in favor of doing something about climate change, or social issues, I've used the meetings I've had thus far
sentences.zh: 但我认为,在座的一些人 都赞成做一些关于气候变化或社会问题的事情, 我利用了至今为止的会议。

sentences.en: to argue in favor of immigration and in favor of climate change.
sentences.zh: 支持移民 支持气候变化

sentences.en: (Applause) And if I hadn't done that, that wasn't on the agenda before.
sentences.zh: (掌声) 如果我没有这样做, 这是没有在议程之前。

sentences.en: So maybe nothing will happen, but at least the words were said.
sentences.zh: 所以,也许什么都不会发生, 但至少有人说了话。

sentences.en: CA: OK. (Applause) So let's talk SpaceX and Mars.
sentences.zh: CA:好的。 (掌声) 那么让我们来谈谈太空X和火星。

sentences.en: Last time you were here, you spoke about what seemed like a kind of incredibly ambitious dream to develop rockets that were actually reusable.
sentences.zh: 上次你在这里,你谈论了 一种令人难以置信的雄心勃勃的梦想 开发火箭,这些火箭实际上可以重新使用。

sentences.en: And you've only gone and done it. EM: Finally. It took a long time.
sentences.zh: 你只做了一次 终于 花了很长时间

sentences.en: CA: Talk us through this. What are we looking at here?
sentences.zh: CA:让我们通过这个。我们在这里看什么?

sentences.en: EM: So this is one of our rocket boosters coming back from very high and fast in space.
sentences.zh: EM:这就是我们的火箭助推器之一 从太空中高速飞来。

sentences.en: So just delivered the upper stage at high velocity.
sentences.zh: 因此,刚刚交付了上级 高速。

sentences.en: I think this might have been at sort of Mach 7 or so, delivery of the upper stage.
sentences.zh: 我想这可能是在马赫7左右, 上层的交付。

sentences.en: (Applause) CA: So that was a sped-up -- EM: That was the slowed down version.
sentences.zh: (掌声) CA:所以这是一个加速的--EM:这是一个减速的版本。

sentences.en: (Laughter) CA: I thought that was the sped-up version.
sentences.zh: (笑)CA:我以为那是快速版本。

sentences.en: But I mean, that's amazing, and several of these failed before you finally figured out how to do it, but now you've done this, what, five or six times?
sentences.zh: 但是,我的意思是,这是惊人的, 和若干这些失败之前,你终于想通 如何做到这一点, 但现在你已经这样做了, 什么,五或六次?

sentences.en: EM: We're at eight or nine. CA: And for the first time, you've actually reflown one of the rockets that landed.
sentences.zh: EM:我们是在八或九点。CA:你已经第一次返回了其中一枚火箭。

sentences.en: EM: Yeah, so we landed the rocket booster and then prepped it for flight again and flew it again, so it's the first reflight of an orbital booster where that reflight is relevant.
sentences.zh: EM:是的,所以我们降落了火箭助推器 并准备再次飞行 并再次飞行, 所以这是第一次 重飞轨道助推器的重飞

sentences.en: So it's important to appreciate that reusability is only relevant if it is rapid and complete.
sentences.zh: 所以,重要的是要认识到 只有在快速和完整的情况下 恢复才有意义。

sentences.en: So like an aircraft or a car, the reusability is rapid and complete.
sentences.zh: 所以,像飞机或汽车, 恢复能力是快速和完整的。

sentences.en: You do not send your aircraft to Boeing in-between flights.
sentences.zh: 不要派飞机去波音机场

sentences.en: CA: Right. So this is allowing you to dream of this really ambitious idea of sending many, many people to Mars in, what, 10 or 20 years time, I guess.
sentences.zh: CA:对了。这让大家可以梦想这个非常雄心勃勃的想法, 将许多人送入火星,大概是10年或20年。

sentences.en: EM: Yeah. CA: And you've designed this outrageous rocket to do it.
sentences.zh: EM:是的,CA:你设计了这枚令人发指的火箭。

sentences.en: Help us understand the scale of this thing.
sentences.zh: 帮助我们了解这件事的规模。

sentences.en: EM: Well, visually you can see that's a person.
sentences.zh: EM:嗯,从视觉上你可以看到,这是一个人。

sentences.en: Yeah, and that's the vehicle. (Laughter) CA: So if that was a skyscraper, that's like, did I read that, a 40-story skyscraper?
sentences.zh: 所以如果那是摩天大楼 我读过吗 40层摩天大楼

sentences.en: EM: Probably a little more, yeah. The thrust level of this is really -- This configuration is about four times the thrust of the Saturn V moon rocket.
sentences.zh: EM: 可能还要多一点,是的。 推力是-- 这个配置大约是土星V号月球火箭的推力的四倍。

sentences.en: CA: Four times the thrust of the biggest rocket humanity ever created before.
sentences.zh: CA:是人类有史以来最大的火箭的四倍。

sentences.en: EM: Yeah. CA: As one does. EM: Yeah.
sentences.zh: EM:是的。CA:就像一个人一样。EM:是的。

sentences.en: (Laughter) In units of 747, a 747 is only about a quarter of a million pounds of thrust, so for every 10 million pounds of thrust,
sentences.zh: 在747单位,747只 约25万磅的推力, 所以每1000万磅的推力,

sentences.en: there's 40 747s. So this would be the thrust equivalent of 120 747s, with all engines blazing.
sentences.zh: 推力相当于120,747,所有引擎都开着

sentences.en: CA: And so even with a machine designed to escape Earth's gravity, I think you told me last time this thing could actually take a fully loaded 747, people, cargo, everything, into orbit.
sentences.zh: CA:因此,即使有一台机器 设计来逃避地球的引力, 我认为你告诉我 上次这件事情 可能真的可以 将一个满载747人, 货物,所有东西, 进入轨道。

sentences.en: EM: Exactly. This can take a fully loaded 747 with maximum fuel, maximum passengers, maximum cargo on the 747 -- this can take it as cargo.
sentences.zh: EM: 完全正确。这可以采取一个满载的747, 最大燃料, 最大乘客, 最大货物在747 - 这可以把它作为货物。

sentences.en: CA: So based on this, you presented recently this Interplanetary Transport System which is visualized this way.
sentences.zh: CA:基于这一点, 你最近展示了这个行星间运输系统, 以这种方式被视觉化。

sentences.en: This is a scene you picture in, what, 30 years time? 20 years time?
sentences.zh: 这是你想象中的场景 30年时间 20年时间

sentences.en: People walking into this rocket. EM: I'm hopeful it's sort of an eight- to 10-year time frame.
sentences.zh: 人们走进这枚火箭。EM:我希望它是一个8到10年的时间框架。

sentences.en: Aspirationally, that's our target. Our internal targets are more aggressive, but I think -- (Laughter) CA: OK.
sentences.zh: 令人感动的是,这就是我们的目标。我们的内部目标更具有攻击性,但我认为——(笑声)CA:好的。

sentences.en: EM: While vehicle seems quite large and is large by comparison with other rockets, I think the future spacecraft will make this look like a rowboat.
sentences.zh: EM:虽然飞行器看起来相当大,而且与其他火箭相比是巨大的,但我认为未来的航天器将使这看起来像一艘划艇。

sentences.en: The future spaceships will be truly enormous.
sentences.zh: 未来的太空船将是真正的巨大。

sentences.en: CA: Why, Elon? Why do we need to build a city on Mars with a million people on it in your lifetime, which I think is kind of what you've said you'd love to do?
sentences.zh: CA:为什么,伊隆?为什么我们需要在火星上 建造一个有上百万人的城市 在你的一生中,我想这是你说过的

sentences.en: EM: I think it's important to have a future that is inspiring and appealing.
sentences.zh: EM:我认为重要的是有一个鼓舞人心和充满吸引力的未来。

sentences.en: I just think there have to be reasons that you get up in the morning and you want to live.
sentences.zh: 我只是觉得你早上起床 想活命是有原因的

sentences.en: Like, why do you want to live? What's the point? What inspires you?
sentences.zh: 喜欢,你为什么想活下去?

sentences.en: What do you love about the future? And if we're not out there, if the future does not include being out there among the stars and being a multiplanet species, I find that it's incredibly depressing if that's not the future that we're going to have.
sentences.zh: 你热爱未来吗?如果我们不在那里, 如果未来不包括在恒星中存在, 并且是一个多板块物种, 我发现如果这不是我们将要拥有的未来,那会令人难以置信地沮丧。

sentences.en: (Applause) CA: People want to position this as an either or, that there are so many desperate things happening on the planet now from climate to poverty to, you know, you pick your issue.
sentences.zh: (掌声) CA:人们想把这个说成是其中之一, 或者说,这个星球上发生了许多绝望的事情, 从气候到贫困,到,你知道,你选择你的问题。

sentences.en: And this feels like a distraction. You shouldn't be thinking about this.
sentences.zh: 这感觉像分散了注意力 你不应该想这个

sentences.en: You should be solving what's here and now.
sentences.zh: 你应该解决这里和现在的问题

sentences.en: And to be fair, you've done a fair old bit to actually do that with your work on sustainable energy.
sentences.zh: 公平地说,你已经做了一个相当老的一点 来做你关于可持续能源的工作。

sentences.en: But why not just do that? EM: I think there's -- I look at the future from the standpoint of probabilities.
sentences.zh: 但是为什么不这样做呢?我从概率的角度来看待未来。

sentences.en: It's like a branching stream of probabilities, and there are actions that we can take that affect those probabilities or that accelerate one thing or slow down another thing.
sentences.zh: 这就像一个分流的概率流, 我们可以采取一些行动 影响这些概率 或加速一件事 或放慢另一件事。

sentences.en: I may introduce something new to the probability stream.
sentences.zh: 我可能会介绍一些新的 概率流。

sentences.en: Sustainable energy will happen no matter what.
sentences.zh: 无论发生什么,可持续能源都会发生。

sentences.en: If there was no Tesla, if Tesla never existed, it would have to happen out of necessity.
sentences.zh: 如果没有特斯拉 如果特斯拉根本不存在 必然会发生

sentences.en: It's tautological. If you don't have sustainable energy, it means you have unsustainable energy.
sentences.zh: 这是陈词滥调。如果你没有可持续的能源, 这意味着你有不可持续的能源。

sentences.en: Eventually you will run out, and the laws of economics will drive civilization towards sustainable energy, inevitably.
sentences.zh: 最终你将耗尽, 经济法则将推动 文明走向可持续能源, 不可避免。

sentences.en: The fundamental value of a company like Tesla is the degree to which it accelerates the advent of sustainable energy, faster than it would otherwise occur.
sentences.zh: 象特斯拉这样的公司的基本价值是它加速可持续能源的出现的程度,比其他情况下的速度要快。

sentences.en: So when I think, like, what is the fundamental good of a company like Tesla, I would say, hopefully, if it accelerated that by a decade, potentially more than a decade, that would be quite a good thing to occur.
sentences.zh: 因此,当我想,比如说,Tesla这样的公司的基本好处是什么,我希望,如果它加速10年,可能超过10年,那将是一件好事。

sentences.en: That's what I consider to be the fundamental aspirational good of Tesla.
sentences.zh: 这就是我认为 特斯拉最有抱负的

sentences.en: Then there's becoming a multiplanet species and space-faring civilization.
sentences.zh: 然后就变成一个多板块物种 和太空文明

sentences.en: This is not inevitable. It's very important to appreciate this is not inevitable.
sentences.zh: 这不是不可避免的 理解这一点很重要

sentences.en: The sustainable energy future I think is largely inevitable, but being a space-faring civilization is definitely not inevitable.
sentences.zh: 我认为可持续能源的未来基本上是不可避免的,但作为一个从事空间活动的文明,绝对不是不可避免的。

sentences.en: If you look at the progress in space, in 1969 you were able to send somebody to the moon.
sentences.zh: 如果你看看太空的进展, 在1969年,你可以派一个人去月球。

sentences.en: 1969. Then we had the Space Shuttle. The Space Shuttle could only take people to low Earth orbit.
sentences.zh: 1969年,我们拥有航天飞机,航天飞机只能载人到低地球轨道。

sentences.en: Then the Space Shuttle retired, and the United States could take no one to orbit.
sentences.zh: 然后航天飞机退役了,美国无法将任何人送上轨道。

sentences.en: So that's the trend. The trend is like down to nothing.
sentences.zh: 这就是趋势 趋势就像一无所有

sentences.en: People are mistaken when they think that technology just automatically improves.
sentences.zh: 人们误以为科技会自动进步

sentences.en: It does not automatically improve. It only improves if a lot of people work very hard to make it better, and actually it will, I think, by itself degrade, actually.
sentences.zh: 它不会自动改善。 只有当很多人非常努力地工作来改善它,而且实际上,我认为,它本身会退化。

sentences.en: You look at great civilizations like Ancient Egypt, and they were able to make the pyramids, and they forgot how to do that.
sentences.zh: 你看伟大的文明 像古埃及, 他们能够制造金字塔, 他们忘记了如何做到这一点。

sentences.en: And then the Romans, they built these incredible aqueducts.
sentences.zh: 然后罗马人建造了这些难以置信的水渠

sentences.en: They forgot how to do it. CA: Elon, it almost seems, listening to you and looking at the different things you've done, that you've got this unique double motivation on everything that I find so interesting.
sentences.zh: 他们忘记了如何做到这一点。CA:伊隆,它几乎看起来, 听你和看着你所做的不同的事情, 你已经得到了这个独特的双重动机 对于我发现如此有趣的一切。

sentences.en: One is this desire to work for humanity's long-term good.
sentences.zh: 一是这种为人类的长期利益而努力的愿望。

sentences.en: The other is the desire to do something exciting.
sentences.zh: 另一点是想做点刺激的事

sentences.en: And often it feels like you feel like you need the one to drive the other.
sentences.zh: 常常感觉你需要一个人来驾驶另一个人

sentences.en: With Tesla, you want to have sustainable energy, so you made these super sexy, exciting cars to do it.
sentences.zh: 与特斯拉,你想有 可持续的能源, 所以你使这些超级性感, 激动人心的汽车做到这一点。

sentences.en: Solar energy, we need to get there, so we need to make these beautiful roofs.
sentences.zh: 太阳能,我们需要到达那里, 所以我们需要做这些美丽的屋顶。

sentences.en: We haven't even spoken about your newest thing, which we don't have time to do, but you want to save humanity from bad AI, and so you're going to create this really cool brain-machine interface to give us all infinite memory and telepathy and so forth.
sentences.zh: 我们甚至没有谈论你的最新的事情, 我们没有时间做, 但你想要拯救人类 从坏AI, 所以你要创造这个很酷的脑机器界面 给我们所有的无限记忆和心灵感应等等。

sentences.en: And on Mars, it feels like what you're saying is, yeah, we need to save humanity and have a backup plan, but also we need to inspire humanity, and this is a way to inspire.
sentences.zh: 在火星上,感觉就像你说的, 是的,我们需要拯救人类 并有一个后备计划, 但我们也需要激励人类, 这是激励人类的一种方式。

sentences.en: EM: I think the value of beauty and inspiration is very much underrated, no question.
sentences.zh: EM:我认为美与灵感的价值 被低估了,毫无疑问。

sentences.en: But I want to be clear. I'm not trying to be anyone's savior.
sentences.zh: 但我想说清楚 我不是想成为任何人的救世主

sentences.en: That is not the -- I'm just trying to think about the future and not be sad.
sentences.zh: 这不是——我只是在试着思考未来,而不是悲伤。

sentences.en: (Applause) CA: Beautiful statement. I think everyone here would agree that it is not -- None of this is going to happen inevitably.
sentences.zh: (掌声) CA:精彩的发言。我想在座的每个人都会同意,这并非不可避免。

sentences.en: The fact that in your mind, you dream this stuff, you dream stuff that no one else would dare dream, or no one else would be capable of dreaming at the level of complexity that you do.
sentences.zh: 事实上,在你的脑海里,你梦到这些东西, 你梦到的东西 没有人敢做梦, 或者没有人能做梦 在复杂的你做。

sentences.en: The fact that you do that, Elon Musk, is a really remarkable thing.
sentences.zh: 你这样做,伊隆・穆斯克, 是一个非常了不起的事情。

sentences.en: Thank you for helping us all to dream a bit bigger.
